title: Online booking cancellation — task plan
summary: Four independently verifiable tasks deliver the approved cancellation and refund-preview requirements in dependency order.

tasks.title: Cancellation eligibility and preview contract
tasks.objective: Expose a deterministic eligibility check and refund preview for a booking before any cancel action is offered.
acceptance_criteria: An eligible booking produces the exact refund amount and currency used by the confirmation step.
A non-cancellable booking returns a user-visible reason and no cancel action.

estimate.rationale: Provider eligibility rules already exist but the preview contract is new.

risks.statement: Eligibility rules differ by booking source.
risks.mitigation: Use the existing policy resolver and add fixtures for each source.

verification: Contract tests cover eligible, ineligible and missing-policy bookings.
Preview amount equals the amount recorded by the confirmed cancellation.

tasks.title: Atomic cancellation transaction
tasks.objective: Persist exactly one cancellation and the displayed refund amount, rejecting duplicate submissions.
acceptance_criteria: Two concurrent cancellation requests produce one accepted cancellation and one idempotent replay.
The stored refund amount matches the preview the traveller confirmed.

estimate.rationale: Follows the existing transaction and idempotency patterns.

risks.statement: A payment-provider timeout can leave the cancellation accepted before the refund is confirmed.
risks.mitigation: Record a pending refund state and reconcile provider callbacks idempotently.

verification: An integration test injects a concurrent duplicate request.
The booking row and cancellation audit record agree on amount and currency.

tasks.title: Cancellation notification after commit
tasks.objective: Queue the confirmation email only after the cancellation transaction commits, without rolling back an accepted cancellation when email fails.
acceptance_criteria: The email job is enqueued exactly once after commit.
A failed email job leaves the cancellation accepted and records a retryable notification failure.
verification: A test replaces the mail transport with a failing stub and asserts the cancellation remains accepted.
Duplicate transaction replay enqueues no second email.

tasks.title: End-to-end acceptance harness
tasks.objective: Provide one reproducible harness that exercises the happy, ineligible and duplicate-cancellation paths for reviewers.
tasks.enabling_rationale: The approved requirements need evidence across the API, database and notification boundary; this harness is enabling work, not new product scope.
acceptance_criteria: The harness runs against a disposable database and reports each requirement criterion with a pass or a concrete failure.
The documented command is deterministic and needs no live provider or forge.

risks.statement: The harness could accidentally depend on live infrastructure.
risks.mitigation: Fail the build if a forbidden network or credential path is configured.

verification: The harness passes from a clean checkout without a live provider.
A deliberately failing expectation produces a non-zero exit and names the criterion.
